page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with one marginal note at the left edge (the dash at mid-page is not text). Running head at the top right above the text. Page number at top left. Greek words set in the body of the text; a final line of text ends at the foot with a partly cut word.

main_text.p: Philippenses profitetur. v. Quod per Timotheum missa legatur Epistola, si fides subscriptioni. Πρὸς Ἐφεσίους γραφὴ ἀπὸ τῆς Ῥωμαίας διὰ Τυχικοῦ. Quanquam ideo haec suspecta est, quod praeter Syri silentium Interpretis, cum absens dicatur fuisse Timotheus, quodque hujus solutionem Hebraeis nunciat, C.xiii,23. Sed alio saltem missus à Paulo colligitur. Aberat enim, & expectabatur Paulo, ἐν Τάξει ἱερᾷ ἀπὸ ἐκ. Utique huic ablegatus, & uti par est, in Macedoniam ad Philippenses, ut non longè antè hac eosdem spe lactarat, Philipp. ii. 19. Atqui ἐν τῷ Paulo ministrare solitus Timotheus, ab uno Paulo mitti & ablegari frequentius. Sic missus ab eo in Macedoniam Act. xix. 22; Corinthum 1. Cor. iv. 17; Thessalonicam, 1. Thess. iii. 2. Nec aliis ministrasse legitur, ipse Apostolorum socius, Ephesiorum jam Episcopus, singulari ratione Paulo obnoxius, necii|sdem cum aliis necessitudinibus junctus.
Author secundi in Epistol. argumenti, apud Oecumenium: οὐδεὶς γὰρ, ὅμως ἐπιλεγόμενον ἐν διακονίᾳ Τιμόθεον, εἰ μὴ ὁ Παῦλος. Nemo opinor.

page.notes: Printed page is a sixteenth-century Latin commentary page with mixed Greek. The Greek is rendered from a low-resolution scan and is uncertain; words marked as partly legible in the Greek lines are best readings. Several words in the first lines are heavily inked and uncertain: "Philippenses" and "suspecta" are read with confidence, but "Ephesiorum" and "necii|sdem" are doubtful and should be checked. Marginal note at left edge and the dash at mid-left are not transcribed as text. Page number "318" printed at top left; running head at top right "De Authore Epistolæ". The text ends with the catchword-like fragment "opinor" partly cut at the foot, so no catchword is given. No signature is visible.
